mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism operates without regime conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% over three consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which typically precedes corporate profit growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5.0% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE falls below 5.0% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real consumption (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days. The interaction is necessary: the effect is only present when both series rise.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise by at least 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST and RSAFS both rise by at least 0.5% from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 days due to recessionary fears. This mechanism is regime-specific to supply contractions.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: A rising CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to central bank tightening concerns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises by at least 2.5% annually.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days. The effect is only present when both conditions hold.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by at least 0.5% and UNRATE falls by at least 0.1pp from prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS rises by at least 0.5% and UNRATE falls by at least 0.1pp.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining GDP growth (GDPC1 annual growth rate < 0.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 days due to recession risks. This mechanism is regime-specific to recessionary demand environments.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 annual growth rate < 0.5%.
